claims.text: Designing fair and motivating algorithmic services requires understanding and accounting for varying fairness notions held by different stakeholders.
Designing fair and motivating algorithmic services requires considering people, contexts, and interfaces for algorithms to function fairly in real-world environments.
Designing fair and motivating algorithmic services requires preserving meaningfulness and social interaction within automated processes.

evidence.description: Stakeholder interviews revealed that findings suggest a need to understand and account for varying fairness notions held by stakeholders.
Stakeholder interviews indicated that algorithms require consideration of people, contexts, and interfaces to work fairly in real-world deployment.
Interviews showed that preserving meaningfulness and social interaction in automation is necessary to build fair and motivating algorithmic services.

methodologies.name: Multi-stakeholder qualitative interview study
methodologies.description: Conducted interviews with multiple stakeholders including staff, donors, volunteers, recipient non-profits, clients, and everyday citizens to inform algorithm, interface, and work practice design.
conditions: 412 Food Rescue donation matching service context

limitations.text: The allocation algorithm design and evaluation are part of an ongoing project focused on a single organization context (412 Food Rescue).
